section_map.heading: ## Summary

section_map.heading: ## How it works

section_map.heading: ## Takeaways
section_map.note: Summary-like restatement of guidance (rule candidates); no ✅ claims.

claim_checks.claim: `private` and `protected` are enforced only during type checking. Runtime lookups, and bracket notation even during type checking, still reach the member: it is "soft private".
claim_checks.page_says: private and protected are only enforced during type checking. ... private also allows access using bracket notation during type checking ... these fields are soft private
claim_checks.note: Runtime access is stated for both private and protected, but the handbook gives the bracket-notation escape hatch and the 'soft private' label to `private` only. The claim widens both to `protected` (wider scope).

claim_checks.claim: `#` fields stay private after compilation and have no bracket-notation escape hatch: they are "hard private".
claim_checks.page_says: JavaScript’s private fields (#) remain private after compilation and do not provide the previously mentioned escape hatches like bracket notation access, making them hard private.

claim_checks.claim: When compiling to ES2021 or lower, TypeScript replaces `#` with `WeakMap`s. The handbook notes that these runtime privacy checks will degrade performance.
claim_checks.page_says: When compiling to ES2021 or less, TypeScript will use WeakMaps in place of #. ... Note that these added privacy checks during runtime could affect performance.
claim_checks.note: The first sentence is entailed. The second raises the handbook's 'could affect' to 'will degrade' (modal raised to MUST level). It also narrows the referent: the handbook's note is about hard runtime privacy mechanisms in general (closures, WeakMaps, private fields), not only the WeakMap downlevel.

claim_checks.claim: Private elements are not properties. They cannot be enumerated, deleted, proxied, or reached through `Object` methods, and `structuredClone()` copies them like public fields.
claim_checks.page_says: they cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method. ... For this reason, structuredClone() does not clone private elements
claim_checks.note: The first part is entailed. The structuredClone part inverts the page: MDN says structuredClone() does not clone private elements.

claim_checks.claim: Reading a `#` field from an object whose class did not declare it throws a `TypeError`. `#x in obj` checks for it without throwing.
claim_checks.page_says: If you access a private element from an object that doesn't have the element, a TypeError is thrown ... You can use the in operator to check
claim_checks.note: The claim's wording matches the error the page prints for C.getX({}): 'Cannot read private member #x from an object whose class did not declare it'. The in operator returns true or false.

claim_checks.claim: V8 9.4 moved class-field initialization, including private fields, onto its inline-cache fast path. Before that it went through slower runtime calls.
claim_checks.page_says: The first issue has been fixed in V8 v9.7 ... Before v9.7, V8 always used a costly runtime call for class field initializations.
claim_checks.note: The page gives V8 v9.7, not 9.4 (wrong version number). The claim also drops the page's condition that the new IC is used only 'when V8 considers the pattern of the initialization to be predictable enough'. The doc's own front matter says V8 ≥ 9.7.

claim_checks.claim: A `#` name cannot be a parameter property (row: injected collaborator → `private readonly x` constructor parameter).
claim_checks.page_says: Allow `#`-private names in parameter property positions ... That this is not possible is a bit surprising
claim_checks.note: The text supports it, but [^5] is a rank 6 issue cited in a role 3 section: a KB-15 breach, recorded separately in violations.

claim_checks.claim: Private elements cannot be proxied (row: object wrapped in a Proxy → `#` access does not go through the proxy).
claim_checks.page_says: While private elements are accessed with the familiar dot notation, they cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method.

claim_checks.claim: TypeScript downlevels it (row: target ES2021 or lower → `#` becomes `WeakMap` lookups).
claim_checks.page_says: When compiling to ES2021 or less, TypeScript will use WeakMaps in place of #.

claim_checks.claim: Working around it with `--experimental-transform-types`: runs on Node 24.22 with an `ExperimentalWarning` (re-tested 2026-11-03); the flag is removed in Node 26.0.0. So code meant to run unbuilt keeps injected collaborators as `readonly #field`s assigned in the constructor.
claim_checks.note: The removal in 26.0.0 is entailed. The page (v26.13.1 docs) says nothing about an ExperimentalWarning on Node 24.22. That rests on a local re-test with no probe. The recommendation in the ✅ cell is the author's inference, not something the page says.

claim_checks.claim: Node only deletes types (row: type stripping stable (stability 2) since Node 24.12.0 and 25.2.0; no warning since 24.3.0; Node ignores tsconfig.json and needs .ts extensions in relative imports).
claim_checks.page_says: v25.2.0, v24.12.0 | Type stripping is now stable. ... v24.3.0, v22.18.0 | Type stripping no longer emits an experimental warning. ... Node.js ignores tsconfig.json files
claim_checks.note: The page also shows 'Stability: 2 - Stable', mandatory extensions ('import './file.ts', not import './file'') and 'Node.js is only removing inline types'.

violations.evidence: C3, item 3: 'will degrade performance' where [^1] says 'could affect performance' (modal raised to MUST level).
C4, item 4: 'structuredClone() copies them like public fields' where [^2] says 'structuredClone() does not clone private elements' (inverted).
C6, item 6: 'V8 9.4' where [^3] says the fix shipped in 'V8 v9.7' (wrong version).
The 'Where each form fits' table cites [^5] (github.com issue, rank 6) for 'A # name cannot be a parameter property' in a role 3 section, which allows ranks 1–4 only.
C1, item 1: the bracket-notation escape hatch and 'soft private' are given to private and protected, but [^1] gives them to `private` only (wider scope).
C10: the 'Runs on Node 24.22 with an ExperimentalWarning' observation and the recommendation are not in [^4]; only the 26.0.0 removal is.
[^6] (TC39 class fields proposal) is never cited in the body, although its entry says 'Backs: How it works 2'.

The section gives a results table but not the benchmark code (no inputs), cites no probe or local artifact, and its measured claims carry neither ✅ nor ⚠️. The Summary ('costs the same as public fields') and Takeaways ('measured cost is nil') restate the measurement as a general rule. The Edge cases row on ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX ('Reproduced on Node 24.22') is also unmarked and has no probe.
A mechanism section also holds a guidance or decision table ('Where each form fits'). The doc has no role 2 (concept architecture) or role 5 (reference) section.
It says 'Verified: 10 claims (✅)', but the body has 11 ✅ marks (How it works 1–6, one table row, four Edge cases rows), and it says 0 unverified while several measured claims are unmarked.
